info.description:
# About the API

All API requests are served from `https://api.mangabaka.org`

Please see the [dedicated API page for general information about the API](/api).

## Response shape

- All API endpoints, whether the request is successful or not, returns a JSON document.
- All JSON documents has a `status: number` root key, designating the status of the response.
  - The `status` field follow the HTTP response code format.
- Error response always have a `message: string` key
  - The `message` field can be safely shown to end-users, as it generally does not contain technical terminology
  - The error response may return additional root keys, please see individual endpoint for more information.
- Results that can be paginated always has a `pagination: object` root key
- Successful requests always contain a `data: object|array` root key
  - `data` is an `array` when the response is listing multiple resources
  - `data` is an `object` when the response is for a single resource

tags.name: Series
tags.description: Public, read-only series metadata: details, covers, relationships, similar, and search.

tags.name: Collections
tags.description: Public, read-only access to a series’ publications: collections, the works (volumes) inside them, and the editions those works are published in. One group because the three are adjacent — a work belongs to a collection, and an edition describes how it was published.

tags.name: Publishers
tags.description: Public, read-only access to publishers and their catalogs.

tags.name: Source
tags.description: Public, read-only lookups of a series by external source id (AniList, Kitsu, MangaUpdates, MyAnimeList, Anime-Planet).

tags.name: Users (/my)
tags.description: Authenticated access to the signed-in user’s library entries and profile.

tags.name: Crawlers
tags.description: Public, read-only crawler traffic mirrored from Cloudflare: which bots fetch the catalogue, how much they take, and what they were served. Cloudflare retains about 8 days of it; anything older exists only because it was mirrored here.

tags.name: Data Moderation
tags.description: Internal moderator/contributor tooling for editing catalog data through the submission system. Versioned v0 on purpose: they expose internal state and may change at any time, without notice or a deprecation window. They are genuinely useful for plenty of automation and tooling, so do use them where they help — just build defensively, pin to nothing, and be ready to adapt when they shift.

id.description: Existing title row id (uuid). Omit/null to create a new title.

is_excluded.description: Remove the title: it stops appearing anywhere, and the row is retained so a future source re-import cannot bring it back at that language. Reversible — clear the flag to restore it.

conflict_resolved_types.description: Which specific conflict types to resolve; required when resolving conflicts.

_key.description: Client-only stable row key for new (id-less) titles; ignored server-side.

_delete.description: Removed. Set `is_excluded` to remove a title; sending this returns 400.

post.summary: 🔒 (stable) Create or update up to 100 library entries (auth: pat or oauth, cache ttl: none)
post.description:
The OAuth token must have the `library.write` scope.
Accepts an array of up to 100 entries; only `series_id` is required per entry and all other fields are optional. Each entry is created if the series is not yet in the library, or patched (only the provided fields) if it is. Every `series_id` must reference an active series (merged/inactive series are rejected). The whole batch is atomic — if any entry fails, nothing is written. The response reports, per entry, whether it was `created` or `updated`. Authentication: requires a Personal Access Token or OAuth (scope `library.write`). Caching: not cached — responses are marked `no-store` for both the CDN and the browser.
